title: SimulationMaxxing: How we ship agents 20× faster — Aman Gupta (Nubank) + Shreya Rajpal (Snowglobe)
talk_summary: Nubank and Snowglobe describe generating synthetic multi-turn agent eval data by wrapping the agent, mocking tools, and driving it with consistent personas, then judging trajectories and feeding results into evals. They claim this shortens release cycles, catches regressions, and lets teams compare models before production AB tests.

takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap the real agent, mock its tools, define personas/use cases, run many multi-turn simulated conversations, then apply per-turn judges and pipe the dataset into the eval pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you get like thousands of multi-turn conversations against your real agents
takeaways.numbers: thousands of multi-turn conversations per simulation run

takeaways.what_they_do: Run candidate open-source and frontier models through the same agent harness and eval setup before committing to a production AB test.
takeaways.evidence_quote: throw a bunch of ideas, open source models at our agent harness and eval setup and see which model versions

takeaways.technique: Known-defect synthetic PRs for reviewer recall
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate simulated agent trajectories with mocked tools and consistent state, then judge behavior per turn to catch regressions before production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we caught a regression uh with simulation that could have made it to production
takeaways.numbers: caught a production-bound regression; one agent TNPS 2x; SSR +4%

takeaways.what_they_do: Compare simulated eval quality against real production data and human domain-expert labels before trusting simulation results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 80% of our domain expert labels confirmed that sims give us usable data
takeaways.numbers: 80% of domain expert labels confirmed sims usable
